goals: mechanistic: quantify how OM respiration depletes dissolved O2 and reshapes inorganic N (NO3/NH4) speciation down a soil column
mechanistic (control variable): resolve how recharge rate governs solute residence time / advection and therefore the redox depth structure
validation: compare simulated pore-water O2 and N profiles to measured chemistry (no in-domain data exists)
key_processes: variably-saturated Richards flow (recharge-driven pore velocity, residence time) — REPRESENTABLE
advective-dispersive solute transport of O2 and N species — NOT configured
aerobic OM respiration / O2 consumption kinetics — NOT configured
nitrification / denitrification redox cascade controlling inorganic N — NOT configured

model_choice.rationale: A single vertical vadose-zone column under prescribed recharge is a PFLOTRAN treatment suite. PFLOTRAN the code supports reactive transport, but the flow-only water bug of the mechanism (O2/N biogeochemistry) is where the mechanism lives.
model_choice.coupling_note: No ELM coupling required; recharge is a prescribed scenario, and the land surface is not the subject.

answerable: recharge-rate control on soil-column moisture content, saturation, pore-water velocity and solute residence time (the FLOW substrate only)

not_answerable.aspect: dissolved O2 depletion by organic-matter respiration
not_answerable.why: PFLOTRAN stack is configured FLOW ONLY — no reactive transport and no microbial/respiration reaction network
not_answerable.needs: reactive-transport + biogeochemical reaction network (O2 consumption kinetics)

not_answerable.aspect: inorganic nitrogen speciation (NO3/NH4) response to recharge and respiration
not_answerable.why: no solute/nitrate chemistry is configured; nitrification/denitrification redox network is absent
not_answerable.needs: multicomponent reactive transport with an N redox reaction network

not_answerable.why: no in-domain solute observations exist AND no chemistry is simulated to compare

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — conceptual recharge sweep on a representative synthetic column (defines only the runnable FLOW substrate)

classes: single representative loam (held fixed for isolation)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Three recharge levels span the low/medium/high factor at a single fixed soil so the recharge effect on velocity and residence time is isolated; N is small because this is a conceptual mechanism-isolation sweep, and because chemistry — the actual question — cannot be run, adding more flow levels would not add scientific answer.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: controlled / not spatial — one idealized 1-D column, vertical domain within the 50 m cap; no DEM/soil raster sampling
sampling_strategy.replication: none — deterministic steady flow, single soil

sampling_plan.reason: long residence time / low pore velocity — the flow endmember where a (missing) reaction network would drive deepest O2 depletion
baseline recharge to anchor the moisture/velocity profile against the two endmembers
short residence time / high flushing — flow endmember where reactions would have least time to proceed

validation_design.target_variable: pore-water O2 and inorganic N profiles
validation_design.observation_source: none in-domain (brief lists pore-water chemistry as missing)
validation_design.comparison: analog — at best a literature/analog check of the FLOW profiles (moisture, velocity); chemistry cannot be validated because it cannot be simulated
validation_design.metric: qualitative consistency with physical expectation (flow only)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: steady prescribed recharge (low/medium/high) on a single representative loam column — FLOW ONLY, chemistry not represented

requires_capabilities.capability: multicomponent reactive transport in the PFLOTRAN column
requires_capabilities.why: the question is about dissolved O2 and inorganic N transport, which the flow-only stack cannot carry
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire O2/N transport core of the question

requires_capabilities.capability: biogeochemical reaction network (aerobic OM respiration / O2 consumption + nitrification-denitrification)
requires_capabilities.why: respiration-driven O2 depletion and N speciation are chemical reactions absent from the stack
requires_capabilities.blocks: the causal mechanism the user asks about

requires_capabilities.capability: organic-matter / substrate specification and microbial kinetic parameters
requires_capabilities.why: respiration rate is the driver of O2 and N dynamics
requires_capabilities.blocks: setting the reaction rates that control the outcome
any validation of the chemical predictions

assumptions: A single representative loam soil is adequate to isolate the recharge effect for the runnable flow substrate; a real design would revisit texture once chemistry is available (texture controls saturation and gas-phase O2 supply).
Recharge treatments are steady prescribed top-flux scenarios within the 50 m domain cap.
The real water table is shallower than 50 m so the column is not pinned at the bottom boundary (unverified — no domain given).
open_questions: Is adding PFLOTRAN reactive-transport + a biogeochemical reaction network in scope? Without it this question is not answerable by the current stack.
What organic-matter content / respiration rate and initial O2/N boundary concentrations should be assumed?
Are there ANY analog-site pore-water chemistry datasets (outside domain) usable for a future reactive-transport validation?
Is a specific soil/climate context intended, or is a fully synthetic conceptual column acceptable?
